title: Agent First Design: kill -9 Halfway Through a Write, and the Data Lines Up Again After Restart | Semantic Tech
description: We killed Cortrix with kill -9 halfway through importing 40 documents. After the restart, every vector matched a block again. Here is what it checks and how to run the test yourself.
imageAlt: Article cover: kill -9 halfway, consistent after restart
sourceDescription: Both experiments in this post are in the Cortrix repo, so you can rerun them on your own machine.

title: Tiger Data Ships a New Vector Index for Postgres, Zep Releases v4, a Paper Finds Agent Memory Won't Fully Forget | Semantic Tech Insights, Oct 19
description: A vector index, two memory platforms and three papers all ran into the same problem this week: deleting agent memory cleanly. Here's what each one shows, and what has to be recorded at write time.
imageAlt: Article cover: Remembering is easy. Deleting cleanly is hard. None of the six memory systems tested in the Bemula benchmark passed more than 1.5% of deletion requests.
sourceDescription: Every item in this roundup links to its public release notes, blog post, or paper in the references.

title: Agent First Design: HTTP 200 Doesn't Mean You Got Everything | Semantic Tech
description: When a Cortrix query can't reach part of what it asked for, it still returns HTTP 200 and says what's missing. See what comes back, how an agent should use it, and when to treat it as a failure.
imageAlt: Article cover: Agent First Design: HTTP 200 Doesn't Mean You Got Everything
sourceDescription: The request and the meta sample in this article come from the Cortrix documentation for v1.0.0-rc.2.

title: Write-Time LLM Inference Gives Every Query More Recall Paths | Semantic Tech
description: Cortrix runs an LLM when a document is written, so context, likely questions, and a document summary each become a recall path at query time. See what we measured and when to enable it.
imageAlt: Article cover: Write-Time LLM Inference Gives Every Query More Recall Paths
sourceDescription: The nDCG@10 figures come from the public Cortrix benchmark evidence pack, pinned to a commit.

title: Cortrix Handles Retrieval. Jev or Laya Can Help the Agent Decide.
description: Cortrix retrieves relevant material and preserves its sources. An agent combines that with current business state, then can use Jev or Laya to assess its next step.
imageAlt: Article cover: Cortrix Handles Retrieval. Jev or Laya Can Help the Agent Decide.
sourceDescription: The article links Jev documentation, Laya source code, and the previous Cortrix article.

title: Vector is not semantic
description: A small retrieval demo separates similarity, ranking, lifecycle checks, and the application rule that decides whether a result is usable.
imageAlt: Comparison of relevance scores and lifecycle status for an old integration guide and a current migration notice

title: Jev and Laya are getting hyped. We're passing for now.
description: Jev can judge a candidate set, but it cannot improve recall. We reviewed the public evidence and decided not to replace Cortrix's local BGE path.
sourceDescription: The launch post introduces Jev. The article also links TypeSafe's reranking cookbook and the two independent evaluations behind the reported numbers.

title: DBpedia explained: why linked data still matters
description: Why stable identities and linked data still matter when your agents retrieve knowledge from different systems.
paperTitle: DBpedia: A Nucleus for a Web of Open Data

title: TransE explained: relationships beyond vector similarity
description: What the simple h + r ≈ t formula tells us about relationships in a knowledge graph, and what a similarity score leaves out.
paperTitle: Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data

title: RAG explained: external memory brings data governance back
description: RAG lets a model use external knowledge. The original paper also helps explain why sources, updates, and data governance still matter.
paperTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

title: Reflexion explained: agent memory without weight updates
description: Reflexion turns feedback into memory without changing model weights. Its most useful lesson may be about the evaluator.
paperTitle: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

title: HippoRAG explained: why RAG comes back to knowledge graphs
description: HippoRAG connects clues across documents with a knowledge graph. Here is how it works, and where the graph can go wrong.
paperTitle: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models

title: Cortrix RC2: 24.4% higher FiQA recall, with Apache 2.0
description: Cortrix RC2 brings 24.4% higher FiQA Recall@10 in the published comparison, Apache 2.0 licensing, and practical ingestion and agent integration fixes.
imageAlt: Cross-encoder retrieval scores in the July and August benchmark rounds
